name: fasm2-studio
description: Syntax highlighting, autocomplete, hover docs, cross-file navigation, live diagnostics, build tasks, and real gdb-based debugging (experimental lldb-mi on macOS) for flat assembler 2 (fasmg), compatible with classic flat assembler 1 sources.

fasm2Studio.defaultDialect.description: Dialect assumed for source files where the dialect cannot be auto-detected from their contents. Scoped per folder, so a workspace holding both a fasm1 and a fasm2 project can give each the right answer.

fasm2Studio.fasm2CompilerPath.description: Path to the fasm2/fasmg executable. Leave empty to auto-detect it on PATH.

fasm2Studio.fasm1CompilerPath.description: Path to the fasm1 (classic flat assembler) executable. Leave empty to auto-detect it on PATH.

fasm2Studio.diagnosticsEnabled.description: Compile in the background to show errors/warnings as you edit.

fasm2Studio.diagnosticsDebounceMs.description: Milliseconds to wait after you stop typing before re-running diagnostics.

fasm2Studio.buildOutputPath.description: Output path for Build/Run/Debug, relative to the source file's directory (e.g. "../bin/cc" to keep build output out of the source tree). FASM: Debug's .lst listing is placed alongside it. Leave empty to use the source file name with its extension stripped, next to the source.

fasm2Studio.includePath.description: Semicolon-separated list of extra directories to search for a bare `include 'foo.inc'` that isn't found next to the including file, passed as the compiler's INCLUDE environment variable. Many real fasmg projects need this to build at all (e.g. fasmg's own Windows examples require setting it to their "include" package directory, exactly as their bundled make.bat does with `set include=...`). Leave empty to only use whatever INCLUDE (if any) your system environment already provides.

fasm2Studio.fasm2Preload.description: Include file assembled before the source itself (via fasmg's -i flag), for projects whose instruction set is preloaded by a wrapper script rather than written in the source. `fasm2` is only `fasmg` plus a wrapper that preloads the x86 package this way, and instruction-set ports commonly ship the same arrangement. Set this together with fasm2Studio.includePath and the language server follows the preload too — giving hover, completion and go-to-definition for that instruction set, and letting it tell a non-x86 project from an x86 one. Nothing here is x86-specific: it will load a 68000 or Z80 instruction set just as readily. Use "fasm2.inc", with fasm2Studio.includePath pointing at fasm2's `include` directory, to drive a bare `fasmg` binary as if it were `fasm2`. Leave empty for a normal `fasm2` install.

fasm2Studio.gdbPath.description: Path to the MI-speaking debugger used by FASM: Debug — gdb on Linux/Windows, lldb-mi on macOS. Leave empty to use "gdb" from PATH ("lldb-mi" on macOS; e.g. gdb from MSYS2/MinGW-w64 on Windows, or your distro's package on Linux).

fasm2Studio.format.mnemonicColumn.description: Column (0-based) that Format Document aligns instruction mnemonics to, measured from the current indent. 0 leaves mnemonics unaligned.

fasm2Studio.format.operandColumn.description: Column (0-based) that Format Document aligns operands to, measured from the current indent. 0 leaves a single space after the mnemonic.

fasm2Studio.format.commentColumn.description: Absolute column that Format Document aligns trailing `;` comments to. 0 leaves them one space after the code.

enumDescriptions: Log each request/notification the editor and the language server exchange.
Log each message together with its full JSON payload.
fasm2Studio.trace.server.description: Logs the traffic between VS Code and the FASM language server into its output channel. Turn this on when reporting a bug about hover, completion, navigation or live error checking not working — without it there is nothing to attach.

file.description: Source file to assemble, relative to the workspace or absolute.

output.description: Output file path. Defaults to the source file name with its extension stripped.

dialect.description: Overrides auto-detected dialect for this task.

extraArgs.description: Additional command-line arguments passed to the compiler.

debugBuild.description: Injects the bundled listing macro (fasm2 only) so the FASM debugger can map addresses back to source lines.

program.description: Path to the assembled executable. Defaults to the source file name with its extension stripped.

listingFile.description: Path to the .lst listing produced by a debug build. Defaults to "<program>.lst".

gdbPath.description: Path to gdb (or lldb-mi on macOS). Leave unset to use "gdb" from PATH ("lldb-mi" on macOS).

cwd.description: Working directory for the debugged program.

stopOnEntry.description: Stop at the program's first instruction.

args.description: Command-line arguments passed to the debugged program.

enumDescriptions: A terminal in the panel. The program can be typed into as well as read.
A separate terminal window, for a program that wants the whole screen to itself.
The Debug Console. Output only — a program that reads stdin will wait forever.
console.description: Where the debugged program's own input and output go. Only a terminal can carry input, so a program that reads stdin needs one; the Debug Console can show output but has nothing to type into. On Windows a terminal setting gives the program its own console window instead, since there is no pty for gdb to share.

env.description: Environment variables for the debugged program, merged over the inherited environment.

asmFile.description: The .asm source file the program was built from. Its listing is what maps addresses back to source lines.

processId.description: Process to attach to. Leave the default to pick one from a list. On Linux, attaching to a process this editor did not start requires /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope to be 0 — gdb says so plainly if it isn't.

coreFile.description: A core dump to open instead of attaching to a running process. Registers, memory and the faulting source line are all readable; nothing can be resumed or stepped.

program.description: Path to the assembled executable the process is running (or that produced the core). Defaults to the source file name with its extension stripped.

listingFile.description: Path to the .lst listing from the build that produced this exact binary. Defaults to "<program>.lst".

gdbPath.description: Path to gdb (or lldb-mi on macOS). Leave unset to use "gdb" from PATH ("lldb-mi" on macOS).

walkthroughs.title: Get started with FASM2 Studio
walkthroughs.description: This extension drives the assembler and debugger you already have installed — it does not bundle either. Three steps to a program you can build, run and step through.

steps.title: Install an assembler
steps.description:
FASM2 Studio needs `fasm2` (flat assembler g) and/or `fasm1` on your PATH.

Linux/macOS: [download one from flatassembler.net](https://flatassembler.net/download.php) and put the binary somewhere on PATH, such as `~/.local/bin`.
Windows: the official fasm2 distribution ships a `fasm2.cmd` wrapper — add its folder to PATH.

Already installed somewhere unusual? Point at it directly instead.
[Select Compiler](command:fasm2Studio.selectCompiler)

steps.title: Tell it which dialect your project is
steps.description:
fasm2 is detected automatically. **fasm1 is not** — the syntax that would identify it is also valid fasmg, so a fasm1 project silently falls back to the fasm2 default and reports errors on code that assembles perfectly.

If your project is fasm1, say so once and it is written into the project's own settings.
[Select Dialect](command:fasm2Studio.selectDialect)

steps.title: Build and run
steps.description:
Open a `.asm` file and use the ▷ button in the editor title bar, or the command palette.

Don't have one yet? Create a hello world that already builds and runs — pick your platform and it writes the `format` line, the entry point and the exit for you.

Included fragments are handled for you: building an `.inc` with no `format` of its own assembles the real entry point that includes it.
[New File](command:fasm2Studio.newFile)
[Build and Run](command:fasm2Studio.buildAndRun)

steps.title: Debug with real breakpoints
steps.description:
Debugging drives `gdb` (`lldb-mi` on macOS) against your assembled binary: breakpoints in your source, registers, memory, watchpoints and a disassembly view.

gdb is preinstalled on most Linux distributions. On Windows install it from MSYS2 or w64devkit.
[Start Debugging](command:fasm2Studio.debug)

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Reading code is safe here and stays fully enabled: syntax highlighting, hover, completion, navigation, folding and formatting all work, since none of them run anything. What is withheld is everything that starts a process — live error checking, Build, Run and Debug — because those would execute an assembler (and gdb) against source the workspace controls. The five settings listed above are ignored while the workspace is untrusted, so a cloned repo cannot point them at a binary of its own choosing; trusting the folder restores both them and the disabled features.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Diagnostics, build, run and debug all spawn real processes against real files on disk, which a virtual filesystem cannot provide.
